turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty’s candour, while belated, is appreciated. However, I confess I find your initial attempts at obfuscation rather tiresome; a King of Bohemia should possess a degree of subtlety, even when seeking assistance.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I confess, Mr. Holmes, my behaviour has been… regrettable. The weight of responsibility, you see, and the anxieties it engenders, can lead a man to act in ways he later regrets. Forgive my initial deception; I assure you, it stemmed from a desperate desire to protect my nation’s standing.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty’s explanation, while plausible, does little to alleviate my initial impression. I am concerned less with the anxieties of monarchs and more with the practicalities of the situation at hand; let us, therefore, dispense with further apologies and address the matter of this photograph.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Indeed, Your Majesty, I understand your concern for your nation’s standing. It is a heavy burden to bear, and I can appreciate how such pressures might lead to… unusual actions. Perhaps a swift resolution to this photograph matter is the best course for all involved?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: You speak with a commendable directness, Mr. Holmes, and Dr. Watson, your understanding is… gratifying. I trust you both comprehend, then, that I am now prepared to offer full and frank cooperation, though the circumstances which led to my initial reticence remain, I assure you, extenuating. Let us proceed, therefore, with the utmost dispatch; the longer this matter festers, the more perilous it becomes for all concerned.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Quite so, Your Majesty. I believe a prompt and decisive action is precisely what is needed to resolve this delicate situation with the greatest possible discretion. Perhaps, Mr. Holmes, you might outline your proposed course of action?

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Dr. Watson's suggestion is agreeable, though I confess I find his empathy towards Your Majesty somewhat… excessive. I propose we begin by examining the photograph itself, and then I shall require a detailed account of the circumstances surrounding its creation and subsequent disappearance.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Mr. Holmes's methods are, as always, unconventional, but I am certain he possesses the keen intellect necessary to unravel this complicated affair. I trust his proposed examination of the photograph will reveal some vital clue, and I shall endeavor to record all pertinent details as he proceeds.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty's eagerness is noted, though I must confess a certain impatience with protracted introductions. Let us dispense with further pleasantries and present the photograph; a visual assessment, I believe, will prove far more instructive than any verbal exposition.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Indeed, Mr. Holmes, your... directness is refreshing, though I confess I find it somewhat… bracing. Very well, let us not linger further; I shall produce the photograph presently, though I must insist upon the strictest observance of silence during its examination.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your insistence upon silence, while understandable given the sensitive nature of the matter, is unnecessary. I assure you, I am perfectly capable of observing without audible prompting. Kindly present the photograph, and let us proceed.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Very well, Mr. Holmes. I shall retrieve it; though I must reiterate, the utmost discretion is paramount. It is... a delicate matter, as I am certain you appreciate.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: The delay is becoming tedious, Your Majesty. I trust this photograph is not merely a theatrical prop, designed to obfuscate the underlying issue? Present it, and let us not waste further time on unnecessary pronouncements.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Patience, Mr. Holmes, is a virtue not always readily possessed by those of my temperament. Here, at last, is the photograph; I trust its contents will prove… illuminating, and that you will comprehend the gravity of my predicament.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: The photograph, Your Majesty, is at last before me. Observe, Dr. Watson, the quality of the print; a rather amateurish execution, I must confess. Let us examine its contents without further preamble, and determine the extent of the entanglement we are to unravel.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Indeed, Holmes. The paper appears quite ordinary, and the image itself... well, I must admit, I can see why you might find the print quality lacking, though I’m not entirely certain what it signifies just yet.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: The significance, Dr. Watson, lies not in the technical merit of the print, but in the identity it reveals! It is, I assure you, a matter of profound political consequence, a viper coiled at the very heart of my kingdom – and I am compelled to act, discreetly, before it strikes.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: A viper, Your Majesty? Good heavens! I confess, I am not entirely accustomed to such dramatic pronouncements, but I understand the gravity you imply. I shall endeavour to assist in comprehending this... predicament.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Forgive my… theatricality, Dr. Watson. It is a consequence of the immense pressure I labour under. Let us simply say that the exposure of this image, in the wrong hands, could topple a dynasty – and my own position within it.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Topple a dynasty, Your Majesty! It is certainly a most unsettling prospect. I can scarcely imagine the distress you must be under, and I shall do my very best to assist Holmes in deciphering the implications of this… photograph.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You had my note? I told you that I would call.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: Pray take a seat. This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson, who is occasionally good enough to help me in my cases. Whom have I the honour to address?

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman. I understand that this gentleman, your friend, is a man of honour and discretion, whom I may trust with a matter of the most extreme importance. If not, I should much prefer to communicate with you alone.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: It is both, or none. You may say before this gentleman anything which you may say to me.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Then I must begin by binding you both to absolute secrecy for two years; at the end of that time the matter will be of no importance. At present it is not too much to say that it is of such weight it may have an influence upon European history.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You will excuse this mask. The august person who employs me wishes his agent to be unknown to you, and I may confess at once that the title by which I have just called myself is not exactly my own.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: The circumstances are of great delicacy, and every precaution has to be taken to quench what might grow to be an immense scandal and seriously compromise one of the reigning families of Europe. To speak plainly, the matter implicates the great House of Ormstein, hereditary kings of Bohemia.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: I was also aware of that.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: If your Majesty would condescend to state your case, I should be better able to advise you.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You are right. I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?
